text:
Small teams ship faster because coordination overhead grows nonlinearly with headcount. A five-person team has ten possible communication paths; a fifty-person team has over a thousand. Every added path is a chance for misalignment, so large teams compensate with meetings, sign-offs, and status docs — none of which produce a working product.

Small teams also carry less decision latency. One person can often decide, build, and ship without waiting for consensus across departments. Ownership is clear, so nobody is blocked wondering whose call something is.

There's also less to protect. Large teams accumulate processes to prevent past mistakes, and those processes outlive their usefulness. Small teams have fewer scars and fewer rules, so they default to action.

Finally, small teams feel their mistakes immediately — bad decisions surface fast and get corrected fast, instead of getting diffused across layers of review where accountability is hard to trace.
